Streaming through Bifrost: a provider slot is held until the upstream sends its first token, not for the whole response, so C is sized from TTFT (measured on kind: 32 slots completed ~160 RPS at TTFT 0.2 s).
Sized from evenly paced arrivals: C and B fit traffic at least this smooth. Real traffic arrives at random and queues more; size from a Poisson stage (load.pacing: poisson).
Utilization ρ must stay at or below 0.8; above it, tail waiting grows sharply.
ρ = 0.849676 is above 0.8, but the run's arrivals were evenly paced and its service near-constant (cv 0.0753135), so no queue formed. Random arrivals would queue at this C.

Streaming through Bifrost: a provider slot is held until the upstream sends its first token, not for the whole response, so C is sized from TTFT (measured on kind: 32 slots completed ~160 RPS at TTFT 0.2 s).
Sized from evenly paced arrivals: C and B fit traffic at least this smooth. Real traffic arrives at random and queues more; size from a Poisson stage (load.pacing: poisson).

A request past position B_max cannot meet the SLO: a larger queue only turns fast failures into slow ones and holds memory. When B_max is small against the bursts, reject when full (drop_excess_requests) with client retries.
ρ = 0.849676 is above 0.8, but the run's arrivals were evenly paced and its service near-constant (cv 0.0753135), so no queue formed. Random arrivals would queue at this C.

To absorb bursts, any buffer up to B_max 79 also meets the SLO; at B_max the working set could reach 499 MiB with headroom, so raise the memory limit to that (the recommended limit is 234 MiB). A buffer past B_max holds only requests that will miss the SLO.
